messages.subject: spiked data
parts:
Hi All,

I'm trying to run some distance models to determine prey density, and one of the species I'm modeling has a large spike in the data directly on the transect (I pasted the histogram below). I've tried binning the data in various ways but the spike remains. The species in question is a white-tailed jackrabbit, which is very cryptic and hard to detect except when flushed, which mainly occurs when you walk right up to them.  Is the distribution of the data such that I shouldn't use distance modeling to determine density?  Is there anything I can do to the data or with various key functions to come up with a reliable density estimate?

Many thanks,

Lucretia

H
i Lucretia,

I don't think that any of the detection functions in unmarked will fit your data very well unless you have some transect-specific covariate that explains the variation in detection distance.

Richard
